REGIONAL GEOLOGY OF

SHANDONG PROVINCE

Brief Text

Shandong Province lies in the eastern coast area of China and the lowerreaches of Yellow River, with its geographical coordinates being from 114°50′to 122°50′ east longitude and from 34°30′ to 38°15′ north latitude. The province, covering a land area of 153,300 km², is geologically a part of the second upwarping and settling zone of the Neocathaysian system. Basically, asound stratigraphic sequence in the geological history can be recognized, anda variety of magmatic rocks and well developed metamorphic rocks are distributed in the province. The famous Yishu fault zone (an important segmentof the Tanlu fault zone) runs through longitudinally in the middle of theprovince. Here, mineral resources are very abundant with oil, gold and diamond well known all over the country. Therefore, the study on the geologicaland metallogenetic characteristics in the area would be of great significanceboth theoretically and economically.

The province, historically, was one of the earliest developed regions ineconomy and culture in our country, with its superiority of physical geographical conditions favorable to thedevelopment of industry and agriculture.

Basically, by the end of 1988, the regional geological survey (mapping onthe scale of 1:200,000) in the whole province had been finished by the Geological Bureau of Shandong (GBS) and the revision of the map sheets andre-mapping (on the scale of 1:200,000) were conducted (with some map sheetsfinished now). Meanwhile, studies on special subjects, such as stratigraphy,tectonics, magmatic rocks and metamorphic rocks in the province werecarried out to improve the understanding of the regional geology. On thisbasis the Shandong Bureau of Geology & Mineral Resources (SBGMR)compiled the REGIONAL GEOLOGY OF SHANDONG PROVINCE at therequest for compiling and publishing the regional geological monographs andrelated geological maps of provinces, cities and autonomous regions by theMinistry of Geology & Mineral Resources. The monograph was...

PDF 538 · 书 534

results obtained from the Comprehensive Research Brigade before 1985, andthe data of reconnaissance survey and mineral prospecting before 1982. Forgeologists at home and abroad, the monograph will be useful as a referencein searching for mineral deposits, in scientific researches and teaching activities and in the development of national economy.

The monograph, apart from the preface, includes five parts, i.e. Part I,Stratigraphy; Part II, Magmatic Rocks and Magmatism; Part III, Metamorphic Rocks and Metamorphism; Part IV, Tectonics; and Part V, GeologicalHistory. It embraces totally 800,000 words, 257 figures, 2 pages of plates, andthe attached Geological Map of Shandong Province, P. R. C. (1:500,000), Magmatic Map of Shandong Province, P. R. C. (1:1,000,000), Tectonic Map ofShandong Province, P. R. C. (1:1,000,000), all of which reflect the currentresearch level of the regional geology in the province.

The content of this brief text is as follows:

PART I Stratigraphy

Shandong is one of the earlier studied regions where there are well developed strata rich in fossils. According to the features of stratigraphic andpalaeontological development, Shandong belongs to the Northern China stratigraphic region and can be subdivided into the Western Shandong (I₂),the Eastern Shandong (Iₐ) and the Northern China Plain (I₃) stratigraphicsubregions (Fig. I-1-1 in the text, the same below). The Changyi-Dadian fault of the Yishu Fault Zone is the boundary between the Western and Eastern Shandong stratigraphic subregions, while the Northern China Plainstratigraphic subregion is bounded in the east by the Liaokao fault which isadjacent to the Western Shandong stratigraphic subregion with its southeastboundary generally running from Yucheng, across Yellow River eastward,through Xiao Qing River, to the Laizhou Gulf.

Western Shandong is the subregion where the strata are best developedas compared to the other subregions. The Archaean Taishan Group is themain component of the strata occurring in the area, which has undergoneregional metamorphism and formed gneisses and amphibolites. Some migmatitic granites and migmatites occurring inthe subregion could have originated from the Taishan Group by migmatization.The Lower Proterozoic Jining Group is composed of slates and phyllites,which were found only in the drill holes in Jining or its vicinity. The Upper

PDF 539 · 书 535

Proterozoic Tumen Group consists chiefly of limestone, sandstone and shale.The Palaeozoic erathem (lacking the upper series of the Ordovician, the Silurian and the Devonian systems, the lower Carboniferous series) forms themain covering strata of the Northern China Platform, overlying unconformably the Taishan Group. The Mesozoic and Cenozoic erathems belong to thefaulted-basin sedimentation, which consist mainly of terrigenous detrital rocksaccompanied with intermediate to basic volcanic rocks, and contain mineralresources, such as gypsum, rock salt, natural sulfur, diatomite, coal, are distributed in the Sishui, Tailai, Xinwen and Yiyuan basins.

The absence of Palaeozoic strata is the most distinctive characteristic ofthe Eastern Shandong stratigraphic subregion where there are only Precambrian and Mesozoic-Cenozoic strata developed. The oldest strata found inthe area are the Archaean-Lower Proterozoic Jiaodong Group or the Jiaonan Group, which are followed by the Fenzishan or the Wulian Group,while the Middle Proterozoic erathem is absent. These three groups contactwith each other by unconformities. The Jiaodong and the Fenzishan groupsare distributed in the stratigraphic minor region of the north Jiaodong Peninsula and theminor region of the south Jiaodong Peninsula. The Penglai Group is found... direction, being muddy, silty and carbonate sedimentation of shallow sea facies.All these rocks have undergone regional metamorphism, and formed the lowto high grade metamorphic rocks which have shaped the crystalline basement. The Mesozoic and Cenozoic erathems are faulted-basin sediments ofchiefly lacustrine, fluviatile and piedmont facies accompanied with intermediate-acidic, intermediate-basic and basic volcanics which crop out in theJiaolai and Huangxian basins.

The Northern China Plain stratigraphic subregion has been completelycovered with the Quaternary System. Except for the Cenozoic strata whichhave been studied in detail in this area, the others were much less studied.Acc...

PDF 540 · 书 536

of fluvio-lacustrine facies deposition and oil-bearing sequence which is quitedifferent from that in western Shandong.

1. Archaean Taishan Group

The Taishan Group, with a thickness of more than 12,000 m, consistsof the earliest strata in western Shandong, covering an area about half ofthe subregion and being mainly composed of hornblendic rocks, gneisses, magnetite quartzite, without typical quartzite and marble. The group has undergone migmatization having formed all kinds of migmatites that are widelydeveloped. B. Willis called it "Taishan Complex" (being chiefly metamorphosed pyrogenetic rocks).

During the period of 1958 to 1961, Shandong Regional Geological SurveyBrigade (SRGSB) set up by the Geological Bureau of Shandong (GBS) and Beijing College of Geology designated the strata as "Taishan Group" which wasbelieved to be metamorphosed miogeosyncline sediments and volcanics, andwas subdivided lithologically into four formations as follows (in ascendingorder):

(1) Wanshanzhuang Formation (Arw), cropping out at the core regionof Mt. Culaishan (徂徕山) and Mt. Mengshan and extending in NW-SE direction, lithologically consists of biotite-plagioclase gneiss intercalated with amphibolite and biotite granulitite, which was the formation of detrital-basic volcanic rocks with 2,000—3,000 m in thickness.

(2) Taipingding Formation (Art), best developed in Mt. Mengshan, ismainly composed of biotite-plagioclase gneiss intercalated with hornblende-biotite-plagioclase gneiss and amphibolite with a thickness of 1,800 to 4,634m which was a detrital-basic volcanic rocks formation.

(3) Yanlingguan Formation (Ary), which commonly has the thicknessranging from 425 to 2,000 m and one of 1198 m in the Yanlingguan area, isdistributed in Tai'an, Xintai, Yiyuan, Mengyin, Yishui counties and is especially developed in Yanlingguan of Xintai County. It consists mainly ofamphibolites, hornblende-schist with the intercalations of biotite granulitite,hornblende granulitite, talc-schist, tremolite-schist and granulitite, being aset of metamorphosed basic volcanic-sedimentary rocks which were originallythe magnesium.

formation at the contact between the lowest portion of the Shancaoyu Formation and the Yanlingguan Formation. The Shancaoyu Formation was argillaceous to basic and intermediate to acid volcanic rocks and has a thickness of 1000—4060 m.

The Taishan Group has been metamorphosed to lower amphibolite facies. Yuqi (ChengYuqi, 程裕淇) and his colleagues (1983) have studied the Taishan Groupin the Yanlingguan area, Xintai, which has further confirmed the sequenceof the Yanlingguan and Shancaoyu Formations, and established the Renjiazhuang Formation at the lower part of the Taishan Group, so it is generallysimilar in lithological characters to the upper part of the Archaean greenstone belts in some other areas of the world. In 1983—1985, a researchteam of the Regional Geological Survey Brigade (RGSB) of the Shandong Bureau of Geology & Mineral Resources (SBGMR) re-investigated the TaishanGroup in the Xinanyu area in Western Shandong where in addition to theYanlingguan and Shancaoyu Formations, the Liuhang Formation was established above them. It is suggested that the Wanshanzhuang Formation bemade up of tonalite, metamorphosed basic to ultrabasic dykes and a zone oftectonic complex which has undergone migmatization and ductile shearing.The Taishan Group has anage of 2,626 Ma as determined by U-Pb isochron method. The Taishan Groupis comparable with the upper Anshan Group (in Liaoning Province) and the DengfengGroup (in Henan Province), with the age older than 2,500 Ma (the late Archaean Era).

2. The Archaean-Lower Proterozoic Jiaodong or Jiaonan Group

The oldest crystalline basement of the eastern Shandong stratigraphicsubregion is composed of gneisses, amphibolites, granulitite and leucogranulitite. During 1958 to 1960 the Jiaodong Group was established, which was subdivided into the Jingqishan Formation and the Huashan Formation. Duringthe period of 1967 to 1968, 805 Team of GBS re-established the Pengkuang (蓬夼),Minshan (民山) and Fuyang (富阳) Formations when they revised the mapping sheets onthe scale of 1:200,000. Meanwhile during the period of 1958 to 1960, theupper Taishan Group was established in the Jiaonan area which was subdivided into the Cangshan, Zhubian and Pingshang Formations. In 1983, theRegional Geological Survey Brigade of SBGMR re-established the Jiaonan Group which was subdivided into the Dashangou (大山沟), Zhenjiagou (甄家沟), Qiuguanzhuang (邱官庄) and Yujialing (于家岭) Formations and assigned to the lower Proterozoic erathem.

But in the present monograph, the Jiaodong and Jiaonan Groups are believed to belong to the Archaean-Lower Proterozoic, above the Taishan Group.

(1) Jiaodong Group (Ar-Pt₁jd)

The Jiaodong Group crops out in the rolling country along the coast ofnorth Jiaodong Peninsula. It has been subdivided according to the representative sections in Menjiazhuang-Jinguoshan (in Penglai) and Beixiaoping (inLaiyang)-Hushan village (in Qixia) as follows.

a. Pengkuang Formation (Ar-Pt₁p), which crops out in Zhaoyuan, Qixia,Tangjiapo, Dazhuangtou and southeastern Penglai areas; with its lower partbeing biotite granulitite and amphibolite, the upper part being biotite schist, the Pengkuang Formation was a set of argillo-arenaceous and basic volcanic rocks and is 4,277 to 12,370 m thick.

b. Minshan Formation (Ar-Pt₁m), which is distributed in Jingqishan (Lai) and is composed ofbiotite granulitite, biotite-plagioclase gneiss, amphibolite, biotite schist andmarble, suggesting the formation a series of clay and semi-clay to carbonate deposition, with minor basic volcanics at its lower portion, being2,259 to 6,957 m in thickness.

c. Fuyang Formation (Ar-Pt₁f), which occurs sporadically in the ChanzhiReservoir (Laixi), with its middle and lower parts being biotite-plagioclasegneiss, hornblende-biotite plagioclase gneiss and less biotite leptite, and theupper part being pimple-shaped and garnet-bearing plagioclase-biotite schist. The original rocks of the formation were argillo-arenaceous sedimentsand intermediate to basic volcanic rock. It's 1,838 to 3,412 m thick.

The formational sequence of the Jiaodong Group consists basically ofthe lower portion of basic volcanic rocks and argillo-arenaceous detrital sediments, the middle portion of calcareous-argillaceous carbonate sedimentsand the upper portion of fine-clastic and silty sediments. The lithology ofthe Jiaodong Group varies widely from place to place, being much more variable in N-S direction than in E-W direction. The degree of regional metamorphism of these rocks ranges from low amphibolite facies, high amphibolite facies to amphibolite-granulite facies. (2) Jiaonan Group (Ar-Pt₁jn)

The group is subdivided into the lower subgroup including the Dashangou and Zhenjiagou Formations and the upper subgroup containing the Qiuguanzhuang and Yujialing Formations. Between the two subgroups thereis a disconformity or local unconformity.

a. Dashangou Formation (Ar-Pt₁d), which crops incompletely out in Jiazishan-, Sishan- and Jufeng (Rizhao City), Taolin (Zhucheng City), Poli (Jiaonan County) and Yushan (Linshu County) areas and is composed of biotite-plagioclase gneiss, biotite-plagioclase-K-feldspar gneiss and biotite granulititeintercalated with marble lenses and amphibolite; its original rocks were theextrusive intermediate to acid volcanic rocks interbedded with basic volcanics of marine facies and small quantity of terrigenous detrital-carbonatesediments; 2,076 m in thickness.

b. Zhenjiagou Formation (Ar-Pt₁z), which mainly crops out along Zhenjiagou (Junan County)-Zhubian-Wangjiadaocunyu-Pengheshi and Suoluo village-Lanshantou, and occurs occasionally in other areas. The lower to middle parts of the formation contain the alternations of biotite-plagioclase-K-feldspar gneiss and muscovite-plagioclase-K-feldspar gneiss, while the upperpart contains biotite schist. Its original rocks were intermediate to acid volcanic rocks; ... min thickness.

c. Qiuguanzhuang Formation (Ar-Pt₁g), which crops well out in otherareas. It is composed of biotite granulitite and leucogranulitite intercalatedwith biotite schist and actinolite schist, of marble by chance, and of quartzite, metamorphosed sandstone and conglomerate near the bottom. It underlies the Yujialing Formation conformably but overlies the Zhenjiagou Formation disconformably or unconformably; 1,091 m in thickness.

A U-Pb isotope age of 1,901—2,182 Ma was obtained from therounded zircons which were collected from the lowest portion of the Qiuguanzhuang Formation (of the upper subgroup), while another isotope age of2,233 Ma was determined by the intersection of the concordia and discordiacurves of the U-Th-Pb method with five zircon samples from the area inthe Ganyu (赣榆) Map sheet (on the scale of 1:200,000). Both the values mentioned above are the metamorphic ages, thus the Jiaonan Group has been assigned to the Archaean-lower Proterozoic.

3. Lower Proterozoic Fenzishan, Wulian and Jining Groups

(1) Fenzishan Group (Pt₁f₂), which is distributed mainly in North Jiaodong. Yang Boquan (杨博泉) first established the group in 1949 in Laizhou City,and later Regional Geological Survey Brigade (RGSB) of the Geological Bureauof Shandong extended the group by including the rocks in the Penglaiarea. RGSBstudied the representative section of the group (in Laizhou City) and dividedit into the upper and lower Subgroups in 1980—1982.

The lower subgroup of the Fenzishan Group is distributed in Pingduof the Danshan anticline) and the Yaochibu-shitouya anticline. The subgroupincludes the Shanzhangjia (山张家) and Mingcun (明村) Formations. The Shanzhangjia Formation consists of the lower part of garnet-graphite schist, the middle of scapolite diopsidite and the upper of feldspar quartzite, with a thickness of433 m; the Mingcun Formation consists of marble and graphite in the lowerportion, garnet-sillimanite schist in the middle, and amphibolite in the upperwith nodular granulitite at the top, with a thickness of more than 1781 m,being the important ore-bearing horizon for graphite, talc, magnesite andiron in the region.

The upper subgroup of the Fenzishan Group, which is distributed in... Zhujiakuang (祝家夼) Formation consisting of rudaceous biotite schist, feldspar quartzite,i) the Zhanggezhuang (张格庄) Formation consisting mainly of marble (3,673 m

thick), (iii) the Jutun (巨屯) Formation of carbonaceous, siliceous and graphite marbles (1,554 m thick), (iv) the Gangyu (岗嵛) Formation of nodular biotite-muscovite schist and tremolite rocks (or tremolite marble) with intercalated biotitegranulitite and feldspar quartzite (over 1,473 m thick) and (v) the Zhifu (芝罘) Formation of rudaceous K-feldspar quartzite, quartz schist and biotite gneiss(1,625 m in thickness).

The lower subgroup is characterized by containing the materials brought up by violent submarine volcanic eruptions on the ocean floor, including those from the upper mantle, and is composed of metamorphosed bimodal calc-alkaline volcanic rocks, various basic and ultrabasic rocks, leptites, gneisses, magnetite quartzite and magnesium-rich carbonate rocks.In terms of regional metamorphism the lower subgroup has mostly attainedto lower amphibolite facies to hornblende-hypersthene granulite facies. Theupper subgroup is made up of quartzites, schists and marbles having resulted from metamorphism commonly of amphibolite facies, and is older than1,900—2,000 Ma as indicated by microfloras and isotope data. So thesubgroup can be correlated with the Hutuo Group in Shanxi Province and the Liaohe Group in eastern Liaoning Province (Table I-3-2).

4. Upper Proterozoic Tumen and Penglai Groups

(1) Tumen Group (Ptatm)

. In 1958—1961, the RGSB of the Geological Bureau of Shandong found at Liguanzhuang, Linyi a bed of basal conglomerate between the Taishan Group and the "Siliceous Limestone" which was situated unconformably above the Taishan Group and disconformably below the Wushan Formation and thus named as the Tumen Formation. On this basis, the Comprehensive Research Brigade of the Geological Bureau of Shandong renamed it as the Tumen Group in 1979 and divided it (in ascending order) asfollows:

a, Heishanguanzhuang Formation (Ptsh), including clay shale, quartz sandstone intercalated with magnetite breccia, 0 to 14 m in thickness;

b, Erqingshan Formation (Ptge), limestone interbedded with sandstoneand shale, more than 280 m in thickness;

c, Tongjiazhuang Formation (Ptat), mottled shale interbedded with thin-bedded limestone, 101 to 493 m in thickness;

d, Fulaishan Formation (Ptsf), quartz siltstone interbedded with thin-bedded marl and sandy limestone, 150 to 217 m in thickness;

e, Shiwangzhuang Formation (Ptas), including thick-bedded calcareousdolomite and dolomitic limestone, more than 121 m in thickness.

The Tumen Group is distributed sporadically in the Yishu fault zoneand its west vicinity (Fig. I-4-2), and contains the representatives of theIV stromatolite assemblage besides Gymnosolen and Baicalia, hence the Tumen Group should be stratigraphically above the Jixian System. Moreover,in the Tongjiazhuang Formation, a microflora of 51 species in all was found,among those the rich ones are Leiopsophosphaera and Trachysphaeridium,etc., which may be assigned to the Qingbaikou System.

(2) Penglai Group (Ptspl)

. The group which is distributed in Qixia-Penglai or their vicinities wasnamed by the RGSB of the Geological Bureau of Shandong. It can bedivided (in ascending order) as follows:

a, Baoshankou Formation (Ptab), slate intercalated with marble andquartzite, 1,071 to 1,275 m in thickness;

b, Fuzikuang Formation (Ptsf), quartzite with bands of siliceous slate. 542

c, Nanzhuang Formation (Ptgn), slate interbedded with marble andmuddy limestone, 1,133 to 1,610 m in thickness;

d, Xiangkuang Formation (Ptsx), including limestone and dolomite interbedded with slate. In 1980—1982, Deng Youhua and Yan Yongkui carried out a stu

5. The Cambrian System

The Cambrian, dominated by carbonate rocks, is distributed in the N.China Plain and W. Shandong stratigraphic subregion, and is developed morecompletely. So it can serve as an early-established and representative sectionin the N. China stratigraphic region which is divided (from bottom to top)into the Wushan, Mantou, Maozhuang, Xuzhuang, Zhangxia, Gushan, Changshan and Fengshan Formations, including 21 trilobite zones. The CambrianSystem overlies the Upper Proterozoic Tumen Group or the Archaean Taishan Group in disconformity or angular unconformity, and underlies theOrdovician Zhifangzhuang Formation in conformity. Due to the developmentof dolomite beds and to the scarcity of fossils near the boundary betweenthe Cambrian and the Ordovician, it is proposed that the gray thin-layeredZhifangzhuang Formation be defined as the lowest limit of the Ordovician.

(1) The Lower Cambrian Series

a, Wushan Formation (∈₁w): the primitive stratotype section at Wushan(Yishui) had no clear connotation, thus the Houjiawo section with completesequence in Liguanzhuang (Linyi) has been accepted as the type section since1976. The lower part of the formation is quartz sandstone, the middle partbeing red brick-colored muddy dolomite and the upper part being thin- tomedium-bedded dolomitic limestone, bearing fossils of Megapalaeolenus zone;

0.7 to 70 m in thickness.

b, Mantou Formation (∈₁m): the stratotype section being at Mt. Mantouin Zhangxia, Changqing County; the main lithology includes red brick-coloured mudstone, muddy dolomite, marl and liver-coloured shale, bearing fo-

ssils of Redlichia chinensis zone; 107 to 219 m in thickness.

c, Maozhuang Formation (∈₁mz): the stratotype section being at Mt. Mantou in Zhangxia, Changqing County; greyish-purple, mica-bearing sandyshale interbedded with oolitic limestone and lenses of bioclastic limestone,bearing fossils of Yaojiayuella and Shantungaspis zones; 31 to 49 m in thickness.

(2) The Middle Cambrian Series

a, Xuzhuang Formation (∈₂x): the stratotype section being at Mt. Mantouin Zhangxia, Changqing County; purplish-red shale and silty shale interbedded with oolitic limestone or sandstone, which locally have been changedinto thick-bedded oolitic limestone, glauconite-bearing sandstone, iron-mica-bearing muddy siltstone and shale, bearing fossils of Hsuchuangia-Ruichengella, Ruichengaspis, Sunaspis, Poriagraulos and Bailiella zones; 73 to 128m in thickness.

b, Zhangxia Formation (∈₂z): the stratotype section being at Hutouyain Gushan, Changqing County; mainly of oolitic limestone, thin clotted limestone, bioclastic limestone, locally interbedded with yellowish-green shales,bearing fossils of Liaoyangaspis, Crepicephalina, Amphoton-Taitzuia and Yabeia-Damesella zones; 98 to 199 m in thickness.

(3) The Upper Cambrian Series

a, Gushan Formation (∈₃g): the stratotype section being at Tangwangzhaiin Gushan, Changqing County; its upper part being alternations of thin-beddedlimestone and muddy-banded limestone in various thickness interbeddedwith bioclastic limestone, wormkalk (edgewise limestone), and the lower partbeing alternations of pimple-shaped limestone and yellowish-green shaleinterbedded with wormkalk, bearing fossils of Blackwelderia zone and of Drepanura zone; 52 to 115 m in thickness.

b, Changshan Formation (∈₃c): the Tangwangzhai section in Gushan, Changqing County being the representative; muddy-banded limestone, medium-bedded algal limestone, wormkalk, thin-plated limestone and yellowish-greenshale, bearing fossils of Chuangia, Changshania-Irvingella and Kaolishaniazones; 70 to 120 m in thickness.

c, Fengshan Formation (∈₃f): the Fanzhuang section in Gushan, Changqing County being the representative; medium- to thin-bedded muddy-bandedlimestone, cloudy limestone, algal-clotted limestone and wormkalk with thefacies having transversely changed into medium-bedded dolomite, bearingfossils of Ptychaspis-Tsinania, Quadraticephalus and Mictosaukia zones; 130to 211 m in thickness.

6. Ordovician System

The Ordovician crops out well in Western Shandong stratigraphic subregion which is carbonate formation of epicontinental sea. The strata, thoughthe upper series is absent, the subregion is a better one for the Ordovician development in N. China. Chen Junyan et al. re-divided the Ordovician in the 1970s and revised the names of the stratigraphic units in 1984, including the Zhifangzhuang, Donghuangshan, Bei'anzhuang and Tuyuformations of the lower series and the Gezhuang and Badouformations of the middle series. The type section is at Wennan, Xintai City.

(1) The Lower Ordovician Series

a, Zhifangzhuang Formation (O₁z): the lower part being purplish-red relict edgewise dolomite and medium-bedded cryptomerous dolomite, bearingfossils—Barnesoceras expansum, Ectenolites penciliformis, Cumberloceras buttsi; theupper part beingband-bearing and meso- to fine-crystalline dolomite and dolomitic limestone, bearing fossils—Yehlioceras yehliense, also Hopeioceras and Coreanoceras; about 110 m in thickness.

b, Donghuangshan Formation (O₁d): yellowish grey microcrystalline dolomite and breccia dolomite, 10 to 87 m in thickness.

c, Bei'anzhuang Formation (O₁b): grey to deep grey, medium- to thin-bedded microcrystalline limestone and medium- to thick-bedded cloudy limestone interbedded with less yellowish-grey thin-bedded dolomitic muddylimestone or dolomite, bearing certain fossils corresponding to the importantcomponents of the Polydesmia zuozhuangensis and Ordosoceras quasilineatumzones previously established; 14 to 90 m in thickness.

d, Tuyu Formation (O₁t): yellowish-grey, thin to medium-bedded micri

8. Permian System

The Permian in Shandong is distributed in the same area as that forthe Carboniferous and belongs to almost the terrestrial facies deposition. Ithas been divided (in ascending order) into the lower series of the Shanxi Formation and the Xiashihezi Formation, and the upper series of the Shangshihezi Formation and the Fenghuangshan Formation.

(1) Shanxi Formation (P₁s): grey to deep grey clay rocks, sandstoneand siltstone interbedded with 2 coal beds minable. It contains plentifulplant remains, including 35 species of 23 genera, mainly of Emplectopteristriangularis, Emplectopteridium alatum, Lobatannularia (?) sinensis, Taeniopterismultinervis, T. nystroemii, Sphenophyllum thonii, S. verticillatum, S. oblongifolium, which coincide completely with those from the Shanxi Fm. in Taiyuan (Shanxi Province), Kaiping (Hebei Province), the Taizi River basin (Liaoning Province) and should be assigned to the early Early Permian.

(2) Xiashihezi Formation (P₁x): yellowish-green and greyish-green sandstone and siltstone interbedded with a small quantity of mottled clay rocks, locally containing thin coal beds or streaks; from the formation havebeen collected plant remains of 19 genera including 37 species, among whichthere are Emplectopteris triangularis, Tingia carbonica, T. partita, T. hamaguchii, Pecopteris arcuata, living in the late Early Permian. The Xiashihezi Formation in Shandong can be correlated with its counterparts inTaiyuan of Shanxi, Kaiping of Hebei and the Taizi River basin of Liaoning.

(3) Shangshihezi Formation (P₂s): divided into 3 members inascending order, i.e. the Wanshan member consisting of yellowish-green sandstone and shale intercalated with mudstone, bearing Bed A aluminousshale at the bottom, the Kuishan member of greyish-white thick-bedded

PDF 552 · 书 548

gritstone interbedded with siltstone and mudstone and the Xiaofuhe member of mottled sandstone and shale interbedded with siltstone and conglomerate; totally 95—490 m in thickness. The plant fossils collected from theformation include 43 species belonging to 20 genera, among which Gigantopteris (?) sp., Gigantonoclea (?) sp., Chiropteris reniformis, Lobatannularia, etc.are common and important elements in the early Late Permian flora of N.China, which may be correlated well with the Shangshihezi Fm. in N. Chinaand the south of North-eastern China.

(4) Fenghuangshan Formation (P₂f): along the north margin of theWestern Shandong upwarping area was continuously deposited a set of redclastic rocks, however, in different places the ratio of sand to mud in sediments varies greatly. For example, the formation consists of 70% of sandstone and siltstone, 15% of mudstone and 15% of sandstones-conglomeratewith a thickness of 370 m in the Dakunlun section, Zibo, or completely of sandstone and conglomerate with a thickness of 448 m in the Longhua section, Zhangqiu, which represents the deposition area close to the sourceregions; whereas the formation is completely composed of sandstone andshale with a thickness of 100 m, which represents the deposition area distant from the regions of alimentation. Although the formation was onceassigned to the Triassic, for the absence of fossils, it is designated to theupper Permian series and is put above the Shangshihezi Fm., in accordancewith the criteria used in "REGIONAL STRATA TABLE OF NORTH CHINA,Shandong Part".

9. Triassic System

Liaocheng Formation (T₂l) is distributed only in the Liaocheng area. Thepetroleum exploration has revealed that it is a series of charophyte- andsporopollen-bearing, purplish-red and brownish-red sandstones, siltstones,mudstones and shales of fluviolacustrine facies, 1245 m in thickness. Theformation has unconformable contacts with both the covering and underlyingstrata and has been dated as early to middle Triassic according to the dataof charophyte and sporopollen fossils.

12. Tertiary System

The Tertiary System in Shandong is a set of terrestrial detrital deposits, developed in the W.Shandong, E. Shandong and N. China Plain subregions. Due to the differences in palaeogeography and in sources of the sediments, the system varies greatly in sedimentation types, lithology, thickness and fauna.

(1) Paleogene System. The system in N. China stratigraphic subregionhas been divided (in ascending order) into the Kongdian, the Shahejie and theDongying Formations.

The Kongdian Formation is composed of brownish-red and greyish-whiteargillaceous sandstone, arenaceous mudstone and sandstone-conglomerate rocks, more than 1500 m thick. The Shahejie Formation is composed mainly ofgrey and deep-grey mudstone with subordinate siltstone and fine sandstone,oil shale and carbonate rocks, partially intercalated with gypsum salt beds;1700—3100 m thick. The Dongying Formation, of alternations of greyish-

In W. Shandong, the Guanzhuang Formation is equivalent to the Wutu

PDF 556 · 书 552

Formation in horizon. The former has been subdivided into three members—Mb. 1 being mudstone, siltstone, sandstone and conglomerate; Mb. 2 being oilshale, siltstone and marl intercalated with thick-bedded gypsum and locallywith rock salt and leopoldite; Mb. 3 being mudstone and sandstone-conglomerate; the total thickness of the formation being more than 2000 m. Thelatter distributed around Changle in the north of W. Shandong, is mainly aset of coal- and oil-shale-bearing detrital sediments: 1000—2000 m thick.

In E. Shandong the Huangxian Formation comprises lithologically greyand deep-grey sandstone and mudstone (bearing oil shale, coal beds), muddylimestone and dolomite with occasionally some sediments of ingression;600—1000 m in thickness.

The Eogene System foregoing bears very rich fossils, including Vertebrata, Mollusca, Ostracoda, Foraminifera, Pisces, Insecta, algae, sporopollen,oncolites and worm tubes left by Polychaeta, etc. The vertebrate faunacan be generally divided into two groups.

(i) the Xintai Group, comprises primarily Kuanchuanius shantungensis, Coryphodon flerowi, Grangeria canina, Hyrachyus metalophus, Heptacodon dubium, which has been found in the middle portion of the Guanzhuang Fm. in Xintai, Mengyin and Laiwu areas, and assigned to the middleEocene.

(ii) the Wutu Group, is composed of Homogalax wutuensis, Changlosaurus reutuensis and Anosteria shantungensis, etc., found in the middle portionof the Wutu Formation in Wutu of Changle and Niushan of Linqu, whichhas been dated as the middle-late stage of the early Eocene.

(2) Neogene System

In N. China Plain stratigraphic subregion, the system has been dividedinto the Guantao and Minghuazhen Formations. The Guantao Formation contains alternations of greyish-green fine sandstone andbrownish-red mudstone in the upper portion, and thick-bedded to massive sandstone-conglomerate with mudstone beds in the lower portion; 150—900 min thickness. The Minghuazhen Formation consists of the upper part of alternations of yellow, brownish-yellow mudstone and sandstone and the lowerpart of mottled mudstone with thin beds of sandstone; 6000—1000 m in thickness.

In W. Shandong stratigraphic subregion, the Neogene is distributed inChangle, Linqu and Yishui and has been divided into three formations: theNiushan Formation, being basalt intercalated with brownish-red mudstone,with brownish-grey and white sandstone-conglomerate at the bottom, 25—

in thickness; the Shanwang Formation, being mudstone, black diato-241 m

maceous shale and oil shale intercalated with olivine basalt, 20—160 m inthickness; and the Raoshan Formation being thick-bedded basalt and basaltic conglomerate, 80—150 m in thickness.

In E. Shandong stratigraphic subregion, the Neogene is distributed inQixia which consists of the lowest part of Tangshanpeng conglomerate—thegold-bearing sandstone-conglomerate being 4—5 m in thickness—and theupper part of Qixia basalt which is iddingsitized olivine basalt being 120 min thickness.

In terms of palaeobiology, two significant biotas occurred during theNeogene Period.

(i) Shanwang Biota, includes a fauna and a flora. The Shanwang fauna contains fossils such as Mammalia, Aves, Reptilia, Amphibia, Pisces.Among them Mammalia is characterized by the presence of the primitiveaceratherids (Rhinocerotidae) and a great number of ceratherids (Rhinocerotidae), of which the significant Stephanocemas, Amphicyon, Lagomeryx, Palaeomeryx and Plesiaceratherium genera were typical Miocene animals on theEurasia and N. America continents. The Shanwang flora is similar to thatof Taidao type in Japan which consists mainly of temperate deciduous plants and of subtropical deciduous broadleaf and evergreen broadleaf ones,corresponding to the present north subtropical plants in the Yangtze Riverbasin of China.

(ii) Pliocene Hipparion fauna from the Balouhe Formation, includeschiefly Hipparion ptychodus, Sinohippus zitteli, Cervavitus demissus, Muntiacus cf. laewustris, etc. which were found in the Zaoyuan-Balouhe area(Zhangqiu). As Hipparion fossils have been found in the middle Pliocene tothe lower Pleistocene in Europe, Asia, America and Africa, it seems there is nodoubt that the Hipparion fauna in the Balouhe Formation can be assignedto the Pliocene but it is difficult to say whether the fauna is equivalent tothe Jingle Stage (early Pliocene) in Hefeng of Jingle, Shanxi Province or tothe Youhe Stage (late Pliocene) in Weinan, Shaanxi Province.

13. Quaternary System

The Quaternary in the province can be geomorphologically classifiedinto that of rolling country and of plain regions.

(1) In the rolling country region

The Quaternary System in the region has been divided, mainly accordingto the relationship of strata, characters of neotectonic movements, isotopic age dating,palaeoanthropology data, buried soil and palaeomagnetic data (in ascendingorder) as follows.

In the lowermountainous areas in Central and Southern Shandong, the formation consists mainly of alluvial and proluvial sediments, glacial and cave accumulations. For example, the proluvia in Xiayuan village, Linqu are fresh-red saprolith and gravel beds; the glacial series in the Taishan district are lodgedboulder clay justified by the landform and lithological characteristic; in theYimeng mountainous area (400—600 m above sea level) the cave accumulations ...Beds.

The Middle Pleistocene series (Q₂) is called the Yuquan Formation in theYishu fault zone which consists of yellowish-brown iron- and manganese-membraned rudaceous beds, also named as "Yellow-skin Gravel Beds", bearing diamonds; 0.5—1 m in thickness. In the Changyi-Qingzhou districtwhere Yang Zhongjian (1934) had established the middle Pleistocene sectionit is red clay, 10 m in thickness. (2) In the plain region

The Quaternary System in the plain region has been studied in detail,and can be divided according to lithology, palaeontology and palaeomagneticdata, as follows (in ascending order):

(i) The bottom of the Quaternary commonly present in the northwestplain of Shandong consists of sand-gravel beds rich in iron. The gravelsare muddy and marly ones, normally 2—5 mm in diameter, subrounded, loosely cemented, locally the sediments are solidified by calcareous cementation.This horizon may be considered as the key bed separating the Quaternaryfrom the Tertiary. In the Jiyang sag the Quaternary is normally 300 to 500m thick; it becomes thicker northward and eastward with the thickest horizon of about 450 m in the Dongying and Xinzhen areas. However it is thinnerin upwarping areas and thicker in sags. The grain size of the sedimentsdecreases from west to east. In the southwest plain of Shandong, the Quaternary has generally a thickness of 150 m with the maximum of about 450 m

PART II Magmatic Rocks And Magmatism

Magmatic rocks are distributed widely in Shandong Province with anexposure area of about 13,338 km² (not including the area of volcanic rocks),accounting for 15% of the total area of crystalline basement.

The magmatic activities can be chronologically grouped into fourstages, i.e., the Archaean Taishanian stage, the Proterozoic Taokeian stage,the Mesozoic Yanshanian stage and the Cenozoic Himalayan stage.

The Late Yanshanian stage is divided into two phases and each phaseinto several sub-phases due to very strong intrusion activities during that time (Table I-1).

The Table I-1 shows that each stage reflects generally a complete tectonicsubcycle within a shorter Period. The Fuping Movement indicated by the angular unconformity between the Archaean Fuping Group and the Wutai Groupin N. China is the major event of deformation in the tectonic cycle. Theunconformity between the Archaean Group and the Proterozoic Group hasnot been found yet in the Yimeng mountainous area of Shandong Province.In spite of this, there is indeed the evidence in the Taishan Group whichindicates the magmatic activities during the Archaean and the Proterozoiceons. For the purpose of dividing the stages and phases of magmatism, theterm Fuping Movement is continuously quoted to indicate the tectonic movement at the end of the Archaean eon.

No matter how long the cycle lasted there is a normal tendency that themagmatic activities evolved from basic to acid, particularly in the Yanshanian stage. Some facts have shown that the volcanic eruptions occurred oftenearlier which were followed by the intrusive activities, and the resultedvolcanic and intrusive rocks perhaps derived from the same magma chamber(s). On the other hand, the magmatic rocks of the Himalayan stage inShandong are not well developed whereas the volcanic eruptions were verystrong which formed basalts covering a large area during the Miocene-Pliocene and Pleistocene. But except dykes, other i

PDF 562 · 书 558

trending structures. The intrusive rocks of different stages are distributedin different tectonic units with the ages of intrusions decreasing from westto east in the province. The intrusive rocks of the Taishanian stage, theearly Taokeian stage and the late Yanshanian stage are distributed intheupwarping area of W. Shandong, whereas in E. Shandong the intrusive rocksof the early and late Taokeian stage, the early and late Yanshanian stageare distributed widely, especially those of the late Yanshanian stage. TheYishu fault zone is characterized by the presence of volcanic-intrusivecomplexes of the late Yanshanian stage.

1, Intrusive Rocks of The Taishanian Stage

The magmatic rocks of the Taishanian stage are referred to as the intru-sive rocks formed by a series of magmatic activities resulted from theFuping Movement. In the early Taishanian stage there were extrusions of astage the crust was uplifted and massive intermediate to basic rocks wereintruded, 'forming migmatitic granitoids covering a Iarger area, includingmainly of the Zouxian granodiorite mass, Zulaishan metadiorite mass andmigmatitic granite mass. In particular, the migmatitic granites are distribu-ted in the broad area of Mts. Taishan, Yishal, Xinfushan and Nishan, etc.,forming a distinctive domain of migmatitic granites in W. Shandong.

The migmatitic granites were transformed from the sial of the crust insitu. The temperature and pressure under which the migmatitic granitesformed were relatively stable. The migmatitic granites have gradationalcontacts with the migmatized metamorphic rocks and, almost without exce-ption, are associated with migmatites and migmatized metamorphic rocks. Inthis area the migmatization was demonstrated by the increase of microclineand quartz contents, the decrease of dark minerals, the transformation ofhornblende to biotite and the decrease of An content of plagioclases in therocks. On the plot showing the relation between 2 Vny and An content ofplagioclase, all the data points fall near the curve of low-teuprature varietyof plagioclase. 2. Intrusive Rocks of The Taokeian Stage

They are referred to as the intrusive rocks formed in accompany withthe Jiaodong Movement and the Fenzishan Movement during the Archaeanto Proterozoic. The rocks intruded into the Jiaodong Group or the JiaonanGroup during the Jiaodong Movement belong to the early Taokeian stage;and those intruded into the Fenzishan Group or the Wulian Group belongto the late Taokeian stage.

(1) The intrusive masses of the Taokeian stage in W. Shandong havemainly intruded into the Taishan Group with intrusive contacts or havemigmatization-metasomatic contacts with it. In the masses there are manyrestites and xenoliths of the Taishan Group and other rock masses of theTaishanian stage. The masses are distributed commonly in NW or NNWstructures. The isotopic age data of the masses vary from 1,754 to 2,075Ma. The Hongdonggou metagabbro mass, the quartz diorites and plagioclasegranites of the Taokeian stage in Puzhaosi, Zhongtianmen and Xianyu-Houpeng are the main representatives.

The Hongdonggou metagabbro mass was formed by three intrusion events; the average content of SiO₂ being 53.76%, the average acidity 3.59, theaverage basicity 16.3, the mafic index M/F = (Mg²⁺ + Fe²⁺)/(Fe²⁺ + Fe³⁺ +Mn²⁺) × 100% = 51.2, belonging to basites. Rittmann's index for the rockis 1.626, the average value of Na₂O/K₂O 2.96 with Na₂O higher than K₂O.

It is distributed in Taishan and Yishan, with the major masses being those in Puzhaosi,Zhongtianmen and Xianyu-Houpeng. In the plot showing the percentage of atomic weight (Fig. II-3-4), 70% samples from the Puzhaosi mass and 91%samples from the Zhongtianmen mass fall into the granite field; on thecontrary, samples from the Xianyu-Houpeng mass fall outside the field ofmagmatic rocks, indicating that the former two masses comprise mostlyremelting granodiorites and the latter, perhaps metasomatic granodiorites.

(2) Intrusive rocks of the Taokeian stage in the north Jiaodongpeninsula are chiefly ultrabasic ones which are distributed in groups andzones in the areas of Sujiazhuang and Pozi in Zhaoyuan County, Malianzhuangin Laixi, Sikou-Tangjiapo in Qixia, Yangjiaogou in Weihai and Wanglianzhuang in Rongcheng County, generally along the axes of basement folds. 3. Intrusive Rocks of The Early Yanshanian Stage

They were intruded into the Jurassic strata and formed before the earlyCretaceous epoch. The time for the intrusion activities lasted 40 Ma (from180 to 140 Ma), i.e. in the early Yanshanian stage which can be dividedinto two phases featured by the intrusive granites.

The intrusive masses in the first phase include the Linglong, Cishan,Queshan, Kunyushan and Wendeng masses, all of which have similar geological features, petrogenetic series and metallogenetic controls. Among thesemasses the Linglong granite mass has been studied in more details.

The Linglong granite mass is situated along the axis of the Qixia anticlinorium with its southwest part extending in NE-direction due to theinfluence of the NE-trending faults. The mass has intruded into the Jiaodong—or the Fenzishan Group. Its U-Pb isotope age being 160 Ma and K-Ar agebeing 191 to 140 Ma. The rock types in the mass include chiefly adamellite,quartz monzonite and granodiorite. In the mass, such minerals as kamacite andmeteoric iron of cosmic origin have been found and feldsparsenclosing sparry iron in the form of small nodular aggregates have been recognized. Theenrichment in δ³⁴S, the oxygen isotope values (δ¹⁸O), +7.4 to +10.43, theinitial ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr ratios, 0.710—0.718. The trace element geochemistry of therocks has shown two characters: (1) the lower Rb content and the higherBa content, (2) the gold abundance is five times higher than the Clarkevalue. The value of ZREE is lower than the average one of granites in theworld, but HREE value has a tendency to be increased as compared tothe LREE value. Moreover, the high Eu/Eu* ratio is an obvious feature.The La/Sm-La diagram drawn according to Taylor's distribution coefficientprinciple is consistent with the model of partial melting for the petrogenesisof the Linglong mass.

The intrusive rocks of the second phase include those of the Guojialingand Mengjia masses which have been studied in detail. The former which isdistrib

4. Intrusive Rocks of The Late Yanshanian Stage

They were intruded into the Cretaceous System and formed before theTertiary. In this stage there were polyphase intrusion events that formedintrusive rocks of polycyclic and polygenic, including those of the Aishan andLaoshan phases.

(1) Aishan phase in which the intrusive rocks intruded into the lowerCretaceous Qingshan Fm. and were later covered by the upper CretaceousWangshi Formation. This phase lasted for about 40 Ma (140—100 Ma).

In Western Shandong the magmatic activity in the Aishan phase beganwith basic intrusion events, reached to the maximum with the formationof intermediate complex bodies and ended with the formation of intermediate to basic dykes (veins). They include the Jinan, Zouping, Laiwu complexesand Chishan alkaline complex. For example, the Jinan complex is a mainlyintermediate to basic one consisting of gabbros, diorites and syenites. It isdistributed in the Jinan-Guodian area and extends in E-W direction. Theearliest horizon intruded by the Jinan complex is the Carboniferous-PermianSystem while nine isotopic age values for the complex range from 276 to82.6 Ma. According to the field contact relationship, three intrusive eventscan be identified with the main body containing three lithological facies. In

the first event were formed gabbros, in the second, diorites, and in thethird, syenites. Either from the inner facies to the border facies of the firstintrusion or from the first intrusion to the third one, the An content ofplagioclases decreases gradually, showing an evolutionary trend from basic toacid, with the degree of order going up obviously and the crystallizationtemperature falling down gradually. In addition, the SiO₂ content of therocks goes up progressively while, on the contrary, the basicity and colourindex fall down gradually; the rocks show an evolutionary trend from basicto acid and from calcareous to calc-alkaline and alkali-calcareous, the degreeof Al enrichment (Al/(Na+K+1/2Ca)) decreases gradually; the chemical composition trend of the rocks evolves from the Mg-Fe²⁺-Fe³⁺- and Ca-richtypes to the Na- and K-rich ones. In addition, the special alkaline Chishancomplex, which is situated in the area between Tanghu of Weishan Countyand Shagou of Zaozhuang City, consists mainly of syenites, alkaline granitesand various kinds of veins; its main part is aegirine-augite-quartz syenite,a small stock stretching in NW-SE direction and dipping to southwest. Dueto alkali metasomatism, minerals, such as albite, acmite-augite, arfvedsonite,Na-rich pyrochlore, thorite and monazite are present in the rocks which,in addition, contain bastnaesite and high contents of rare earth elements ofcerium family. The rocks have the average SiO₂ content being 68.53% andthat of Fe₂O₃, FeO, CaO and MgO being less than 2%, and hence belong toacid rocks; as the average association index value (α = (Na₂O+K₂O)/(SiO₂-43)) indicates, therocks belong to the calc-alkaline rock series. Moreover, a small amount ofstandard mineral aegirine is present.

In E. Shandong, distributed are mainly intermediate-acid and acid rockswhich occur as composite masses. The Aishan composite mass is a representative among them, which includes adamellite-granites in Mts. Aishan andZhuajishan. In the tuffaceous sandstone-c

In one word, the Aishan and Zhuajishan massesare similar and related to each other in terms of mineralogy and chemicalcomposition, assuming they originated from the same magma chamber, i.e.adamellite magma chamber which was formed in the depth by remeltingand was similar to granodiorite in composition. The magma migrated upduring tectonic movements (mainly faulting), evolved (mainly by differentiation) continuously in the course of migration and solidified into masses ofdifferent composition—the Aishan paraporphyritic adamellite and the Zhuajishan dense-porphyritic adamellite in different time and different geologicalconditions.

Intrusive rocks in the Yishu fault zone are best developed in the Tongjing area where they occur mainly as small intermediate and acid stockswith a few small intermediate to basic stocks, consisting chiefly of biotitegranodiorite, adamellite porphyry and norite-gabbro.

(2) Laoshan phase, to which the rocks having intruded into Mb. 2 andcovered by Mb. 3 of the Wangshi Formation of the upper Cretaceous areascribed. They are predominantly acid and alkali-acid granites comprisingsingle or composite mass(es). The Laoshan mass (with isotopic age of 101—132 Ma) is the best representative. According to its lithologic feature andcrosscutting relationship among individual intrusions five intrusive eventshave been recognized in which a series of alkali-granites were formed. The amounts of main oxides of porphyritic kimberlite,including SiO₂, TiO₂, Al₂O₃, FeO, Fe₂O₃, P₂O₅, are similar to Daly's; theSiO₂/Mg ratio is near 1 which is generally similar to the chemical compositions of kimberlite in other provinces of the world, MgO content is lowerwhile CaO content is higher than Daly's. The chemical compositions of thefine-grained kimberlite vary widely because phenocrysts and accessoryminerals in the rock are not distributed evenly; the chemical compositions ofautochthonous fragments are more uniform.

In short, magmatic rocks of the late Yanshanian stage can be dividedinto two classes of the Aishan and Laoshan phases, which are the productsof different phases in the same tectonic-magmatic cycle. They are differentbut are related to each other by progressive evolution which was a continuous and irreversible process.

5. Intrusive Rocks of the Himalayan Stage

They occur only on a small scale, chiefly as ultrabasic and basic dykesin Shandong. The ultrabasic dykes are distributed in the area of Xujialiugou, Xujiapandian of Fentuan in northeastern Juxian and belong to brecciatedalkali-picrite-porphyrite, intruding into porphyritic syenites of the late Yanshanian stage and trending in NWW direction. Petrochemically they belongto the alkali-ultrabasic rocks of potash-series and are similar to alkali-ultrabasic nephelinite of the Cenozoic volcanic rocks in Shandong. In addition,there are also some basic dykes distributed in W. Shandong, such as diabasedykes in Yiyuan.

6. Mode of Formation and Source Materials

Magmatic rocks in Shandong were manifold and polygenic in terms ofthe mode of formation and their source materials. They can be classifiedinto three genetic series: (1) mantle-derived series, (2) remelting geneticseries of mixed source materials which, according to the source materialsforming the rocks, can be further divided into two genetic subseries: (i)remelting genetic subseries of mixed source materials consisting mainly ofcontinental crust material with some mantle-derived material participatingin; (ii) syntexis genetic subseries of mixed source materials chiefly comprising of mantle material with some crust material participating in; (3)crust-transformed genetic series which, according to the contact relationship,i.e. whether the masses had moved or not, can be subdivided into (i) autochthonous granites of the crust-transformed types, (ii) parautochthonousgranites of the crust-transformed type.

Magmatic rocks in Shandong Province are mostly those of the remeltinggenetic series of mixed source materials, especially predominated by the remelting genetic subseries of mixed source materials, secondly, of the crust-transformed genetic series. The magmatic rocks of the three genetic seriesevolved in parallel with each other, particularly the remelting genetic seriesand crust-transformed genetic series were often evolved contemporaneously,related with each other but developed independently.

7. Mineralization

Magmatic rocks in Shandong were influenced by basement materials andhave obvious mineralization. The gold mineralization which is closely relatedto the granites occurring chiefly in the early Yanshanian stage, while Cu.the late Yanshanian stages iron mineralization is closely related to the intermediate to basic intrusions and also occurred mainly in the Yanshanianstage, other types of ores are closely conriected with the magmatic rocks ofthe late Yanshanian stage as well.

PART III Metamorphic Rocks And Metamorphism

1. Metamorphic Rock Types and Restoration of Its Original Rocks

The metamorphic rocks in Shandong Province are very complex, whichare widely distributed in the pre-Cambrian terranes, and each group has itsOwn characteristic rock association.

The green-schists in the Taishan Group are distributed mainly in Yanli-Yanlingguan Formation occur in great thickness and in bands, most of themare green, greyish-green and greyish-white in colour, showing schistose stru-cture, and lepido-nematoblastic, nematoblastic, granoblastic and prismatobla-stic textures, their original rocks were mainly ultrabasic lavas and basicvolcanic rocks. Komatite has been found in the ultrabasic lavas and its ty-pical chemistry shows that Si0z= 46-53% (or greater than 45%), Al20g lessthan 10%, Mg0=10-20% (or more than 9%), K20 less than 0.9% and Ca0/AlzOs ratios equal to or lager thaln one, the An content of plagioclases pre-sent is higher than 30. Hornblendes are chiefly green with some being blui-shgreen in colour. The main rock types are chlorite-tremolite schist, chloriteschist, actinolite schist, tremolite schist, chlorite-actinolite schist, biotite-acti-rolite-schist, talc-chlorite-tremolite schist and serpentine-chiorite-tremolitescbist,etc.

Armphibolic rocks which are exposed in the areas of Taipingding of Mt.Mengshan, Mt. Xinfushan, Yanlingguan of Xintai, and Wande of Jinan areof the Yanlingguan Formation, they include amphibolite, hornblende-plagio-clase gneiss, amphibole schist and hornbendite, generally the rocks show

Blastovesicular (wormtube-shaped), blastoamygdaloidal, blastodiabasic, blasto-tholeiitic and blastoporphyritic textures. Their protoliths belong to basiclava, pyroclastic rocks and basic intrusive rocks.

Gneiss rocks are more common in the Minshan and Fuyang formationsof the Jiaodong Group, and include biotite-plagioclase gneiss, hornblende-plagioclase gneiss, hornblende-biotite-plagioclase gneiss, sillimanite-garnet-biotite-muscovite-plagioclase gneiss, sillimanite-bearing garnet-biotite-K-feldspar gneiss, garnet-bearing kyanite-biotite-plagioclase gneiss, the protoliths of aluminium-rich or graphite-bearing gneisses are mostly argillaceous rocks, thoseof hornblende-bearing biotite-plagioclase gneiss are chiefly quartz-andesite,andesite, andesite-basalt lavas and pyroclastic rocks.

Granulites of the Jiaodong Group are mainly distributed in a belt fromLaixi, through Pingdu and Changyi, to Anqiu, which lies in the south flankof the Qixia anticlinorium. They include leucocratic granulite and hornblende-two pyroxene granulite, often associated with diopside-plagioclase amphibolite, diopside amphibolite and amphibolite, crystals of apatite and zircon inthe rocks are characteristically rounded, the crystal cores and edges arerounded or disappear with the ratio of length to width being 1:1. Someof the protoliths of the rocks may be, in part, basic volcanic rocks.

Eclogites distributed in the Jiaonan Group have their own characteristicsand always occur in the Zhenjiagou Formation in a small size of several toover ten meters long (with the longest one less than one hundred meters),as stratiform-like, lenticular and orbicular bodies in shape. Sometimes eclogites are also distributed as veins in ultrabasic rocks, such as in augite peridotite, garnet-pyroxenite and pyroxenite with a gradational contact relationship, and also in ultrabasic rocks, such as augite-peridotite or olivine-pyroxenite with either abrupt or gradational (or intercalation) contact relationship.

The Fenzishan and Wulian groups consist mainly of marbles and, inaddition, of garnet-bearing sillimanite-biotite schist, sillimanite-biotite schist,lumped tourmaline-bearing sillimanite-biotite-quartz schist, andalusite schistand chloritized plagioclase-biotite schist, etc.

The tourmaline-bearing sillimanite-biotite-quartz schist which showslepido-granoblastic texture and schistose structure occurs mainly as interlayers and is composed of quartz (30-35%), plagioclase (20-25%), biotite(25-30%), sillimanite (15-20%) with a small amount of tourmaline and raremagnetite and zircon; sillimanite occurs as prisms, hairy or sheaf aggregates,and makes up the main component of the lumps in the rocks; tourmaline, with its well-developed transverse fissures, occurs as anhedral prisms. schist is often changed into gneiss facies, suggesting that its protoliths maybe aluminium-rich clay rocks.

Andalusite-biotite schist occurs mainly in the Haiyankou Formation inDazhuzishan of Wulian County, and is blackish to dark-grey in colour. Itshows porphyroblastic and lepidoblastic textures and schistose structure. Themineralogy of the rock includes biotite (40%), andalusite (30%), quartz (25%)and carbonaceous matter (1%). Andalusite occurs as porphyroblasts whilebiotite shows pleochroism: Ng-brownish-red, Np-yellowish. Under microscopethe rock shows blastopsammitic texture and zircon is rounded. On the petro-chemical diagrams the data points of the rock are located in the region ofsedimentary rocks, so its protoliths may be clay and argillo-arenaceous sediments.

The Penglai Group is composed mainly of pebble-bearing quartzite, quartzite, phyllite-slate, slate and marble-limestone, which exhibit well-developedbedding structure, blastopelitic and blastoaleuritic textures. They belong tolow-grade metamorphosed sedimentary rocks.

2. Characteristics of Migmatization

(i) The regional metamorphic rocks of the Archaean Taishan Grouphave generally been subjected to intensive migmatization, forming partialmigmatite, migmatite and migmatitic granite, etc. which are distributed inMts. Taishan-Zulaishan, Xinfushan-Wujianshan, Mengshan, Fenghuangshan,Nishan, Yishan and Lushan, occupying about 4/5 of the total basement area.

Rocks with different degrees of migmatization show a zonal distributionand from center to outside, the migmatization intensity decreases gradually.In the migmatitic centres are dominantly distributed migmatitic granite andmigmatitic granite gneiss, which are replaced successively by nebulite, homogenic migmatite, striped migmatite and augen migmatite outwards and thenby weakly migmatized regional metamorphic rocks further outwards. Thezonation is parallel to the regional lineament, and each centre correspondsgenerally to the anticline axis of the basement. According to the distributionof the centres there are several migmatitic fields, such as the Nishan-Baiyan-, Mengshan-, Northern Feicheng-, Taishan-Zulaishan-Xinfushan-, Ma'anshan-Lushan-Haoshan- and Wengqan-Gongdanshan-Fulaishan migmatitic fields (Fig. Ⅲ-2-7).

The matrices (palaeosomes) of migmatites are mainly biotite and hornblende rocks, whereas the veins (neosomes) are felsic, cryptomerous and granitic rocks. After migmatization, SiO2 content of the rocks increased, andNa2O and K2O contents also increased to some extent whereas componentssuch as Fe2O3, FeO, Al2O3, MnO, MgO, TiO2 and CaO have been taken away

to various extent. With intensive migmatization, the quantity of microclineand quartz in the rocks has gradually increased with microcline up to25--50%, and quartz moxe than 20% the An content of plagoclases decrea-sed from andesine (An= 30-45) to oligoclase (An=14-28): and the arnountof biotite decreased (abous 5-8%); plagioclase has been replaced bymicrocline and progressively by albite, while perthite and nyrnekite haveforrned, hornblende has been replaced by biotite, which, in turn, with Ti and Feremoved,could have been metasomatized and converted to sphene and magnetite.In the intensively migmatized rocks in the Nishan area, the restites of porp-hyro blastic and schlieren migmatites often occur. The schlieren migmatite hasbeen covered by migmatitic granite in the Taipingding Formation in Namia-oshan and Qingyunshan areas, which suggests that there were two stages ofmigtnatization. The analysis has indicated that the first stage of migmatiza-tion is featured by potassium metasomatism with great intensity ani widematism (locally prominent Na-metasomatism) which is restricted to the str--ucturally favourable positions-migmatization centers where the two stageshave been superimposed onto the rocks.

(2) The migmatization jn the Late Archaean-Early Proterozoic Jian-dong or Jiaonan Group has been less intensive and on a much sinaller scalerocks have often formed. The Dashangou Formation and part of the Zhenjia-gou Formation of the Jiaonin Group belong to migmatitic geniss or homo-genic migmatite. The charactcristic of mignuatites in the lower Fenzishansubgroup of Proterozoic is similar to that in the Jiaodong Group. The mig-matization in the upper Fenzishan subgroup has been weak which is repre-sented by injections of felsic-, quartz- and pegmatite veins while metasoma-tism has been very weak. The fact that the regional migmatization has notaffected the Late Proterozoic Penglai Group reflects a trend that the olderthe metamorphic strata are, the more intensive the migmatization is.

Plagioclase all belongs to andesine (An=30-35); biotite is mainly dark-reddish-brown and partly brown in colour. Diopside-bearing mineral associationsare common in metamorphosed basic rocks, in which diopside has a smoothand straight contact with other minerals and hornblende is always dark-bluish-green to bluish-green in colour; plagioclase all belongs to andesine (An=30-35) and biotite is reddish-brown in colour. The metamorphic pressuresand temperatures were estimated to range between 4-7 kbar and 525-560℃,respectively, by the hornblende-plagioclase pair in quartz-bearing amphibolite, thus it can be assigned to the high amphibolite facies of medium-pressure facies series.

The rocks of low amphibolite facies crop out in the north part of Zhaoyuan, Mouping, Weihai, Rushan and Wendeng areas, mainly in the JiaodongGroup which lies on the north side of the "Qixia Anticlinorium" axis and tothe east of the Taocun fault. The rocks can be divided into two associations.The lower association consists mainly of biotite leptite and amphibolite withits top being staurolite-bearing almandine-biotite schist, the upper one comprises biotite-plagioclase gneiss, hornblende-biotite-plagioclase gneiss intercalated with bands of amphibolite, garnet-biotite schist and diopside marble. In the metamorphosed pelites, plagioclase belongs to oligoclase (An=25some diagnostic metamorphic minerals, such as staurolite and kyanite, also exist. The mineral assemblage of metamorphosed basic rocks is hornblende + plagioclase + quartz. The metamorphic temperatures and pressures wereestimated from the hornblende-plagioclase, hornblende-garnet and biotite-garnet mineral pairs inthe rocks, so they belong to the low amphibolite facies of medium-pressurefacies series.

(3) The metamorphic grades of the Jiaonan Group, from high to low,are as follows: low amphibolite facies, high greenschist facies, and low greenschist facies, which all belong to the medium-pressure series. The intensityof metamorphism for this group is closely related to the age of the strata.

The rocks of low amphibolite facies crop out widely in the Qiaozishanarea of Rizhao, and are also distributed in Taolin (Zhucheng)-Poli (Jiaonan)area in the north, and in Yushan (north Linshu) in the south of the area

. 573

PDF 578 · 书 574

The representative metamorphic strata are the Dashangou Formation, of whichthe upper part consists of mica-two-feldspar gneiss, hornblende-plagioclasegneiss with bands of leucogranulitite, muscovite-quartz schist and amphibolitewhile the lower part, of biotite-plagioclase gneiss, biotite-plagioclase granulitite intercalated with amphibolite- and marble lenticles. The study of itsmineral assemblage has shown that epidote is absent in the metamorphosedbasic rocks and plagioclases are oligoclase-andesine. The metamorphic pressure is estimated to be 6-6.5 kbar and temperature 525-580℃, which are withinthe range of low amphibolite facies of medium-pressure series.

The rocks of high greenschist facies are distributed in the southernLinshu-Pingshang (Junan) area and the Taolin (Zhucheng)-Qibaoshan (Jiaonan) area. The typical metamorphic strata are those in the Zhenjiagou Formation, of which the lower part consists of two-feldspar gneiss, muscovite-two-feldspar gneiss with leucogranulitite bands,while the upper part comprises biotite schists. As for the mineral assemblagein these rocks, hornblende has replaced actinolite and plagioclase belongs tooligoclase; in addition, there are some associated minerals, such as epidoteand garnet. The metamorphic pressures and temperatures are estimated to be3-6 kbar and 500-570℃, respectively, belonging to the range of high greenschist facies of medium-pressure series.

The rocks of lower greenschist facies are those in the QiuguanzhuangFormation and the Yujialing Formation. The former is chiefly composed ofbiotite granulitite and leucogranulitite intercalated with biotite schist andactinolite schist; the latter consists mainly of biotite schist, actinolite schistand mica granulite with bands of marble and quartzite. In terms of mineralassemblage, amphiboles present are mainly tremolite and actinolite, which areassociated with albite and epidote. The metamorphic pressures and temperatures are estimated to be 3-6 kbar and 350-500℃, respectively, belongingto the range of low greenschist facies of medium-pressure facies series.

(4) Metamorphic facies series in the Fenzishan Group

(i) The lower subgroup of the Fenzishan Group belongs to the amphibolite-granulite facies of medium-pressure facies series and is distributedin Nanshu of Laixi County, Liangmu and Malan of east Pingdu, Mingcun ofwest Pingdu, Zuoshan of Changyi and Zhaogezhuang of Anqiu. The rock association of the metamorphic strata is composed of garnet-bearing sillimanite-plagioclase gneisses and biotite granulitite intercalated with thick bands ofolivine marble, feldspathic quartzite, graphite gneiss, diopside-amphibolite,hornblende-two-pyroxene granulite and two-pyroxene granulite, etc. In metapelites the mineral assemblage of sillimanite + K-feldspar occurs widely, whi-

plagioclase belongs to the more basic andesine (An=4f), biotite is dark-brown,occurring as prismatic crystals and hairy aggregates which are the products derived frobiotite. In some metabasites the mineral assemblage of hypersthene + diopsidehas also occurred; in some metamorphosed basic rocks plagioclases are andesine-labradorite (An=40-60); hornblende, dark-brown or greenish-brown incolour. [Figure caption:] Diagram showing the relationship between the unit cell parameter a0 of Ca-rich almandine and the grade of metamorphism, the data points of the rocksall fall into the sillimanite and kyanite fields. The common presence ofsillimanite and kyanite and the coexistence of two pyroxenes and plagioclasein the metamorphic rocks suggests that the rocks correspond approximatelyto the medium-pressure facies series.

(ii) The upper subgroup of the Fenzishan Group belongs to the lowamphibolite facies of medium-pressure facies series, and is distributed in the areasof Fushan, Penglai and Fenzishan of Laizhou. The metamorphic rock assemblage consists of biotite granulitite, mica schist, staurolite-kyanite-garnet-biotite-muscovite schist and tremolitite interlayered with various kinds ofmarble, diopsidite, amphibolite and graphite-bearing rocks. Although theoccurrence of hairy sillimanite in nodular biotite schists of the Gangyu Formation and in staurolite-bearing kyanite-garnet-biotite-muscovite schists ofthe Zhifu Formation can not be considered as a basis for classifying the rocksinto the high amphibolite facies, it is suggested that the rocks have reachedat least the low amphibolite facies. In pelitic rocks, occurring plagioclases areoligoclase-andesine (An=32), biotite is yellowish-brown and brown in colourand garnet is common, whereas in metabasites hornblende is bluish-green togreen and plagioclases are oligoclase and andesine (An=21-33). Due to theoccurrence of staurolite and kyanite the metapelites can be classified as thestaurolite-kyanite metamorphic zone.

(5) The Wulian Group belongs to the amphibolite facies of medium-to low-pressure facies series and crops out on the north side of the Haoguanzhuang-Puluogu fault; this group can be approximately correlated withthe upper subgroup of the Fenzishan Group.

(6) The Penglai Group is mainly distributed in the areas of Qixia andPenglai and the Miaodao islands. The metamorphic rock association comprisesquartzites, slates, marbles and limestones, etc. According to the mere occurrence of sericite and chlorite in the metapelites, it can be classified as sericite-chlorite zone. Moreover, it belongs to the monofacies, i.e., the low green-
