PART IV Tectonics

1. Latitudinal Structural System

Around latitude 34°20′—35°13′N, the north branch of Qinling latitudinalstructural system is developed as a belt from Heze-Tengzhou-Zaozhuang, across the Yishu fault zone, to Zhubian-Pingshang-Ganyu, which consists mainlyof the Fengpei convex, the Jinteng concave, the Taozao basin and a groupof nearly EW-trending folds and faults, mainly including the Heze-, Fushan-, Yutai-, Chanxian-, Taozao-, Xiangdi-Dafangqian and Nanshihe-Xidouling faults, with associated N-S-trending extension faults, such as the Jiaxiang-, Sunshidian- and Yishan faults.

The latitudinal structural system was active as early as pre-Sinian time, but then attenuated during the Palaeozoic; it became violent again in theMeso-Cenozoic.

2. Regional EW-Trending Structural Belts

To the north of the latitudinal structural system mentioned above, severalinterval of 30′—35′ (about 60—65 km), including (from north to south):

(1) the Penglai-Huangxian belt,

(2) the Qixia belt,

(3) the Pingdu-Jingangkou-Shidao belt,

(4) the Laiwu-Yiyuan-Jiaozhou belt,

(5) the Wenshang-Sishui belt.

Except the Qixia belt, all of them are distributed discretely, scatteredand developed weakly in Shandong Province. The Qixia regional EW-trendingstructural belt has been very active and has had its basic form since pre-Sinian time, whereas the others were formed during the Meso-Cenozoicmainly by faulting and associated deposition.

3. Regional NS-Trending Structural Belts

The NS-trending structural belts are not well developed in the province. Most of them occur as tectonic slices, or locally, as discontinuous belts,including:

(1) the Tengzhoudianzi-Shanting-Guanqiao fault belt,

(2) the Yuwangshan-Cangshan structural belt,

(3) the Laomuzhuhe fault belt in Eastern Shandong.

PDF 581 · 书 577

The regional NS-trending structures occur mainly as faults, some ofthem were filled with the Meso-Cenozoic veins. They didn't come into beinguntil the late Mesozoic, so the NS-trending belts belong to the weakeststructural system in the area.

4. Neocathaysian System

The Neocathaysian System is the dominant one that is best developed inthe area. The Yishu fault zone is a typical example. Two groups of faults(shear planes) associated with the Neocathaysian System are also well developed, which include those of the Taishan pattern, such as the Tai'an-Dawangzhuang fault (embraced by a brush structure in W. Shandong), the Xiawei-, Shanxiangjia-Haoguanzhuang-, Xiaoguan-Fengcheng- and Daguangfu-Fujia faults, and of the Dayishan pattern including the Yidu-, Jiushan-,Hanwang-, Jinxingtou-, Wenzu- and Changqing faults, etc.

The Neocathaysian NNE-principal-compressive-plane is accompanied by two groups of the NNW-trending (Dayishan pattern) and NE-trending (Taishan pattern) faults, which, in the province, emerged in the Jurassic, underwent many movements and finally were shaped in the late Eogene. The Neocathaysian System has been formed by the Meso-Cenozoic movements in the province. Its dominant part, the Yishu fault zone, had experienced a continuous left-handed compresso-shear movement for a long time,but then was transformed to a rift due to the left-handed extension whichresulted from the upwelling of upper mantle materials as the faultsdeeply cut through the crust and reached to the mantle in the Cretaceous.The fault zone underwent a violent compresso-shear movementagain in the Eogene, which lasted until the Quaternary. Therefore, the Yishu fault zoneis not only an important component of the Tanlu fault zone, but also a great fault zone in Eastern China.

It begins from Tancheng, through Central Shandong, approximately following the Yihe, Shuhe and Weihe rivers and then goes into the Bohai Sea with a length of 330 km. Its south and north ends are covered bythe Quaternary sediments

As a typical representative of the Neocathaysian System, the Yishu faultzone continued its left-handed rhaegmageny for a long time, which produceda series of associated structures resulting from rotation and shearing, suchas the Northern Shandong brush structure, the Western Shandong brushstructure and the "S"-shaped structure in northwest Jiaodong peninsulaThe fault zone outcrops discontinuously and extends for 250 km in NNEdirection (10°—25′) with the average strike of 17°; it is about 60 km wide 577

PDF 582 · 书 578

in the north but only 20 km in the south, and has a clear outline on theLANDSAT image (Fig. IV-1-8).

The Yishu fault zone consists primarily of four major faults, i.e., theTangwu-Gegou-, the Yishui-Tangtou-, the Anqiu-Juxian- and the Changyi-Dadian faults, which in turn, from west to east, form a pattern of two grabens intervened by a horst in the middle, with the north and south endsbounded by the Meso-Cenozoic depressions. Folds are rare in the fault zone,but some open folds are developed in the Mesozoic depressions in

it. The major faults in the Yishu fault zone have been often intersected byEW-, NW- and NE-striking faults, so that some of them occur as brokenlines in plan view, which also reflects a feature of strong movements sincethe Mesozoic and has had a control over the deposition of the Mesozoicstrata and magmatic activity. Moreover, many secondary faults making upthe major ones are complex in nature, including normal-, reversed-, thrust-and transverse faults. The step normal faults (Babaozhuang), the imbricatedthrust faults (local assemblage in Wangjiamiao, Shaohuyu) or the normaland reversed faults (Shijing) can often be seen in the same section. Thecompressive normal faults (Kuaibaozhuang, Wanjiamiao) are unique in theYishu fault zone.

The common occurrence of fault slices between some secondary faults isanother diagnostic feature of the Yishu fault zone. The slices may consistof the Taishan Group, the Tumen Group, the Palaeozoic or the Meso-Cenozoic sediments, such as the Meso-Cenozoic slices between the faults F1 andF2 (Jishan, Wangjiazhuangzi).

The same major fault may occur in different style in different areas.For example, the fault F1 occurs, in turn, from north to south as a crumpled zone (Zhenwumiao), a sub-buried fault bunch (Wangjiamiaozi, Shijing), and the exposed single major fault (Yishuhe), which suggests that thedisplacement along the fault F1 has been gradually increasing from north tosouth since the Cretaceous.

The fault zone has controlled the intrusion (Shijing) and eruption (Shaohuyu, etc.) of magmas, especially of basic, ultrabasic magmas and xenoliths through the crust and reaches the upper mantle.

The fault zone has experienced intensive neotectonic movements andhence is an important earthquake-controlling fault in Eastern China (asshown in Shijing, Jishan and Jizhuang).

It is very likely that beneath the Yishu fault zone is an upwarped

PDF 583 · 书 579

Aeromagnetic data have shown that the depth of Mohorovicic discontinuityin the west of the Tangwu-Gegou fault is about 35-36 km (Fig. IV-1-10);it is only 25 km in the region between the Tangwu-Gegou and Yishui-Tangtou faults and is no less than 36 km in the Eastern Shandong block to theeast of the Changyi-Dadian fault. According to the results of magnetotelluric sounding in the Linyi area, with the Changyi-Dadian fault as a boundary, the electric conductive layer of the upper mantle beneath the EasternShandong block (to the east of the Yishu fault zone) lies at a depth below300 km, whereas that beneath the region to the west of the fault zone at a depth of onlyover 70 km; this also indicates that the Changyi-Dadian fault isa great deep fault reaching the mantle (Fig. IV-1-12).

As the Yishu fault zone is an important fault zone in Eastern China, itis of great significance to learn its formation and development; therefore, many geologists have made investigations on it, but have had various ideas

fora long time. Some believed that the fault zone could have formed as early as in the Archaeanor the Proterozoic and experienced mainly vertical movements which controlled the strata developed in Eastern and Western Shandong. Others believed that it experiencedleft-handed strike-slip movements. However, there is still a dispute on thequestion as to how much the strike-slip displacement could be. At first, basedon the aeromagnetic survey data, someone assumed the displacement to be100 km; later, according to the offsets of geologic bodies on the oppositesides of the fault zone, others suggested the distance ranging from 200 kmto 740 km. Although ideas were proposed one after another, so far none hasbeen accepted unanimously.

5. North Shandong Brush Structure

It is considered that the W. Shandong upwarped region is the backboneof the North Shandong brush structure. The vortical layers from outer toinner are, in turn, the Huanghua depression, the Chengning rise and theJiyang depression;a part of the Chengning rise lies in Shandong Province.

The Huanghua and Jiyang depressions were mainly formed in the Eogene period when the oil source rocks deposited there. There are a series ofsecondary en echelon rises which, like the Chengning rise, are made up of; thedepressions become younger in age gradually from south to north, as well asthe oil source rocks, that is, there was a migration of deposition centres in

PDF 584 · 书 580

the vortical layers of this brush structure away from the backbone.

This is a buried giant brush structure covered completely by the Neogene and Quaternary sediments. It is composed of three compressional vortical layers produced by the counter-clockwise rotation of the Western Shandong block in the Eogene due to the left-handed wrench movement of theYishu fault zone.

6. West Shandong Brush (Vortex) Structure

The West Shandong vortex structure is developed in the Western Shandong upwarped region and is well exposed. Its backbone is the Nishan dome, while its vortical layers are a number of depressions and rises bounded bysome faults. The major faults include the Tai'an-Dawangzhuang-, Tongyedian-Sunzu-, Lianhuashan-, Xintai-Duozhuang-, Wensi- and Mengshan faults. The rises, depressions and faults occur in alternations, which shows afeature that the Meso-Cenozoic depressions are bounded in the north byolder rocks toward the south . The vortex structure is a clear arc projecting northward and converging southeastward.

On the rises are distributed the Taishan Group and a little Palaeozoicrocks, while in the depressions occur the Meso-Cenozoic sediments of severalthousand meters thick.

The vortex structure is closely related to the long-term left-handed wrench movements of the Yishu fault zone with a complexhistory.

7. "S"-shaped Structure in Northwestern Jiaodong Peninsula

It lies in the Laizhou-Zhaoyuan-Qixia area and includes principally theSanshandao-, Huangxian-Laizhou-, Zhaoyuan-Pingdu- and Xilin-Douya faults. Except for the Sanshandao fault which is mostly covered by the Quaternary sediments, all faults are well exposed, making up a prominent "S"-shaped structure.

The faults show distinct compresso-shear nature and are accompanied bysmall brush structures nearby, such as the Linglong brush structure.

In the province, several well-known large to ultra-large gold depositsarehosted just in the major and derived secondary faults.

In the early stage of the Yanshanian movement, the Yishu fault zonestructure which controlled the intrusion of magmas and the formation of goldore deposits .

8. Cathaysian Structural System

PDF 585 · 书 581

The Cathaysian structural system occurs mainly in the Moupin-Jimo line.which runs through the centre of the Jiaodong peninsula, and consists ofthe Taoling-Doushan-, Guocheng-Jimo-, Zhuwu-Dianji-, Haiyang-Qingdaoand Rushan-Liugezhuang faults.

The fault zone exhibits clear compressional aad compreso-shear featureand is characterised by left-handed wrench movement with the maximumdisplacement up to 30 kmi. The taults appear to occur at more or less equalinterval of 10--12 km.

This structural system was probably developed following the older NE-trending structure and had its activity in the Jurassic. However, the mosthave occurred in the late Yanshanian Stage or the late Cretaceous and waslikely to have lasted until the Eogene. Its movement might be related to theactivities of the Yishu fault zone.

9. * 人"-type Structure in Eastern Shandong

It accurs in the Jiaobei, Jiaonan uplifts and the Jiaolai depression,and is convex northwestward to some extent, spreading as an arc in Jiaodongpeninsula.

The Jiaolai depression is narrower in its north portion and becomeswider southwestward, forming an open "L"- shaped depressiondivergingsouthwestward. It neighbours with the Changyi-Dadian fault and the sedi-mentary basins in the depression are connected with each other. The Meso-zoic sedimentary-lithofacies distribution in the Jiaolai depression suggeststhat the sedimentary' center kept inigrating from southeast to northwestwith the sedinments overlapping the Jiaobei uplift.

The “人"-type structure was active during the late Jurrassic to the lateCretaceous, or even to the Eogene. The faulting and magmatism took placemainly on the uplifts whereas the late Jurassic-Cretaceous volcanism andnormal sedimentation occurred chiefly in the depression.

10. Basement Structure

The basement structure is probably a giant "drag arc'.

The “Drag arc" pattern;the left-handed strike-slip of the Yishu faultin pre-Sinian time dragged the Nw-trending Taishan Group and the nearEW-trending Jiaodong and Fenzishan groups, respectively, resulting in anwu-Gegou fault was developed at the apex of the ancient dxag arc in W.Shandoag that changed the strike of the Taishan Group in the Yishu faltzone into the NE and NNE directions.

PART V Geological Evolutionary History

During the long history of geological development Shandong has expe.rienced many strong tectonic movements and yarious geological processes.With its own characteristics, Shandong shared the same unit with the North:China platform. In the monograph we intend to discuss the geologicalevolutionary history of Shandong since the Mesozoic era in terms of thetectonic (structural) systems. As the palaeo-structures prior to the Mesozoicare difficult ta restore, the pre-Mesozoic geologic evolution of Shandong is:analyzed and synthesized based on the geological-historical records, as.reflected fron the sedimentation, magmatism, metamorphism and tectonismin Shandong, and on the isotopic chronologic data., The geological evolutionhistory is described successively with respect to the Archaean-Proterozoictime, the Palaeozoic, the Mesozoic and the Cenozoic eras.

1. Archaean-Proterozoic Era

Changyi-Dadian fault of the Yishu fault zone, a series of geological events.with great difference have taken place. They are listed in Table V-l.

Up to ncw,there is still a dispute over when the Changyi-Dadianwith continous activity and its age could dated back to the Archaean orthe Proterozoic. Featured by the vertical movements, the Western andEastern Shandong blocks experienced, in turn, subsidence and uplifting,receiving deposition or being eroded. As a result, the Archaean TaishanGrouP, the lower Proterozoic Jining Group and the Upper Proterozoic Tumen.Group of the Qingbaikou System have been developed in W. Shandong,whereas the Archaean-Proterozoic Jiaodong Group, the Lower ProterozoicFenzishan Granup or Wulian Group and the upper Proterozoic Penglai GroupPdeveloped in E. Shandong. Others believed that it was a Mesozoic faultwhich has had strong movements since the Mesozoic era, and has been aleft-handed wrench fault zone with a displacement of 100 km, or 200 km,or even740 in different opinions, It is likely that the fault may be a collision boun-dary between the two different geological blocks, for which the evolutionaryhistory of Western and Eastern Shandong will be discussed separately.

(1) Western Shandong Region

On the supracrustal rocks in W. Shandong deposited the Taishan Group

PDF 587 · 书 583

tions consist of argillo-arenaceous and volcanic rocks, whereas the YanlingguanFormation—basic volcanic rocks, and the Shancaoyu Formation—argillo-arenaceous rocks. By the end of the Shancaoyu deposition period, the Taishan Group underwent amphibolite-granulite subfacies regional metamorphism in the Xintai stage,which was associated with the regional migmatization, forming the Taishan-,Yishan-, Lushan-, Mengshan- and Nishan migmatite domes. Most of the Taishan Group was converted into migmatitic granite, homogeneous migmatite andpartial migmatite. With the termination of the Fuping Movement, the basement of Western Shandong uplifted and underwent erosion continuously,resulting in the absence of the strata prior to the Jining Group or thoseequivalent to the Wutai of the Jiaodong Group. During this uplift and erosion theregion underwent the following events: in the first event, under the action of NE stress, were formed the Cishanrock bodies; in the second event, under the intensive NE-NNE stress field, were induced the NW-trending thrusts along which developed the Zhongtianmen intermediate to acid intrusions.

During the early time of the Early Proterozoic era, an aulacogen appearedin the west margin of the Taishan continental nucleus. It developed furtheras a linear trench and received argillaceous, argillo-arenaceous deposits andintermediate volcanics—the Jining Group, which, then, was subjected togreenschist-facies regional metamorphism, followed by the Taokeian magmatic intrusions. The crust was uplifted and subjected to erosion and planation,resulting in the absence of sedimentation in the late Early Proterozoic-Middle Proterozoic period. In the early Late Proterozoic, under the further NScompression, the Taishan continental nucleus was subjected to the longitudinal tension while the Yishu strait formed, which was gradually connectedwith the Qingbaikou sea spreading in Jiangsu and Anhui regions, and thenthe Tumen Group deposited.

In the early Sinian time, as the Yishu strait rose, there was no sedimentation there, as well as in the W. Shandong upwarped area, from the Sinianto pre-Wushan formation time of the Cambrian.

In South Jiaodong, the Dashangou Formation of the early Jiaonan Stage(lower Jiaonan Subgroup) was composed of intermediate to basic and basicvolcanic rocks—medium clastic formation; the Zhenjiagou Formation—intermediate to acid volcanic rocks—medium clastic formation. The basicvolcanic rocks mentioned above are generally equivalent to the oceanicbasalt, whereas the intermediate to acid rocks, to the island-arc andesite ofbathyal-abyssal facies along the continental margin. In the late JiaonanStage (upper Jiaonan Subgroup), the sedimentary environment was greatlydifferent from that of the early stage. The Qiuguanzhuang Formation wascomposed of intermediate to acid volcanic rocks (intercalated with intermediatecarbonates)—argillaceous to fine clastic formation . The depositional environment was featured by frequent vibration of the crust with the dramaticvariation in thickness of lithofacies, so it may belong to volcano-tectonicbasin and shallow sea environment.

In North Jiaodong, the Jiaodong Group is considerably different fromthe Jiaonan Group. The Pengkuang Formation of the Jiaodong Group consistsof basic-intermediate to basic volcanics and sedimentary rocks with only alittle change in lithofacies thickness, and carbonates occur as lenses. Thissuggests that a large area in North Shandong was initially subsiding, formingan epeiric sea-bathyal environment, and later, the crustal differential movementbecame enhanced. The Minshan Formation is a suite of clay, clayey to carbonate sediments with basic volcanic rock bands. The Fuyang Formation belongsto clastic-intermediate to basic volcanics formation with the thickness ofthe beds varying substantially, and several different lithological beds occur in thesame horizon, which change gradually to one another along the strike ordip, suggesting there was a volcano-tectonic basin, or gulf, or lagoon environment.

Although the Jiaodong and Jiaonan groups show significant lithofacieschanges, they have similarities in terms of sedimentary and tectonic environment.

With the increase in thickness of sedimentary pile and in temperature,the sediments underwent regional greenschist-amphibolite-facies metamorphism.As in a few anticlines and faults the heat flow went upward successively, the migmatization became stronger and the homogeneous migmatite on the

PDF 591 · 书 587

Baowuding anticline thus formed. Under the NS compressional stress, theEW-trending (or latitudinal) structures accompanied with some intrusions, suchas the Suoluoshu ultrabasic bodies of the early Taokeian Stage and theYuejishan granites, which were unconformably overlain by the FenzishanGroup. This is named as the Jiaodong movement.

In the Early Proterozoic, the active crust was changed gradually into astable one in the region where the Fenzishan Group deposited as clasolite,turned to be a new extensional environment in which rift, graben andhorst formed in early time of the Early Proterozoic, then followed by the development of trenches where the Fenzishan and Wulian groups deposited.

By the end of the Fenzishan Stage the Fenzishan and Wulian groupsunderwent medium to high grade regional metamorphism, followed by upwarping, being subjected to, at least twice, the N-S compressions and yieldingthe tight overturned folds in the lower Fenzishan Subgroup and the openfolds in the upper subgroup in EW-trending. The Fenzishan Group hasbeen overlain by the Penglai Group by unconformity, which stands for theFenzishan movement, whereas the Middle Proterozoic and the QingbaikouSystem of the Upper Proterozoic are absent in the region.

During the Late Proterozoic (the Sinian), the area in the north of thePenglai-Fushan line started to subside and received deposition of the Penglai Group which was an ingressional series of sandstone-mudstone-carbonate,having been metamorphosed into quartzite, slate and crystalline limestone.After the Penglai Group had risen, a series of EW-trending open foldsformed, which occurred as monoclines in places and were inherited from the[……脱字]。The regionwas under a long-term uplifting and eroding state until the Mesozoic whenit began to receive new sediments.

2. Palaeozoic Era

The Eastern and Western Shandong regions were in remarkably differentenvironments in the Palaeozoic. The E. Shandong underwent continuouserosion, while in the W. Shandong formed a series of marine strata consistingmainly of carbonates in the Early Palaeozoic and a set of coal measures.This indicates that the Western Shandong region was a platform featuredby oscillatory movements and devoid of magmatic rocks at that time.

3. Mesozoic Era

As Shandong is situated between the second uplift zone and the second

(I) In the Triassic, the Neocathaysian Liaokao fault moved first, theeast block to the fault continued uplifting and erosion, so there was no.Triasic sedimentation there, whercas in the Dongming-Linqing depression.in the west of the fault deposited the Triasic Liaocheng Formation.

(2) In the early to middleJurassic, the Neocathaysian Yishu andLiaokao faults were undergoing continuously the left-handed strik-slipmovement, As a result, a series of NNE-trending depressios and uplifts.formed in Dongming-Linqing faulted basin while the NEE-trending basins:(Zibo and Fangzi) formed in the north margin of the W, Shandong upliftedarea, where deposited are the important coal measures (e. g. the FangziFormation) and the Santai Formation.The Yishu fault zone continued itsuplifting and left-handed shearing that changed the early, near NS-trending.Yisu fault zone into an important Neocathaysian fault zoe. Because the warm and moist climate was suitable forliving things to grow, plants, such as Psilophyta of Goniferae were mostflourishing at that times while Vertebrata, such as Pisces, evolved to itshigher stage. At the end of the late Jurassic, the Linglong. Kunyushan andQueshan granite masses emplaced along the Neocathaysian faults.

( 4) In the Cretaceous the Yishu fault zone was still active, undergo-ing left-handed tenso-shearing movement in which developed the Anqiu-Juxian and Yishui-Tangtou faults bounding the Mazhan-Sucun and Anqiu-Juxian grabens, the"人"-type strucure system in E, Shandong and the brushstructure system in W. Shandong developed further on the original backgro-und that controlled the deposition of the Qingshan and Wangshi formations.

During the Qingshan period, there were three volcanic eruptive cycles withcomplex styles, including either central eruptions or fissure eruptionss andfrom south to north and from west to east. In addition, sub-alkaline voica-aic rocks occurred in some places.

The intrusive activity in W. Shandong was relatively weak which formedmainly small rock bodies of calc-alkaline and ultra-alkaline rock series. On.the contrary, the intrusive rocks in E. Shandong were most developed,including mainly those granites formed in the Aishan phase, with which.some important onferrous metal ores were assocaited.

In the Wangshi period, mainly red sandstones and conglomerates of.fluviolacustrine facies with well-preserved fossils, such as Tanins, Helopuszdanskyi were deposited.

By the end of Cretaceous, this region was extensively uplifted andsubjected to erosion that led to the folding and inclination of local bedsaccompanied with magmatic intrusions of the Laoshan phase and sometimeshydrothermal polymetallic ore fillings (veins) occurred.

Conclusions

The monograph was compiled based on the results of the regional geological surveys (on the scale of 1:200,000) in Shandong which have beenalready finished and on the full use of other important data and achievements from the prospecting and exploration for mineral resources and from theanalysis of the data obtained according to the modern geological theory. Wehope that the research of the regional geology of Shandong will be advanced

and problems are summarized.

Some progress hasbeen made. 2. In this monograph, we have classified the magmatic rocks in Shandong into the Taishanian, the early and late Taokeian, the early and lateYanshanian and the Himalayan stages, and discussed their distributions indifferent tectonic units. There is a general trend that the ages of magmaticrocksdistributed in the W. Shandong upwarped area formed mainlyin the Taishanian Stage, the early Taokeian Stage and the late YanshanianStage, whereas those developed in the E. Shandong upwarped area formedmainly in the early and late Taokeian Stage, the early and late YanshanianStage in particular; those in the late Yanshanian Stage are well developed.The magmatism in Shandong is featured by polyphase activities whichwere controlled by tectonism. This is especially true for the late Yanshanian granites which can be divided into the Aishan phase and the Laoshanphases, the former includes three pulses of intrusions and the latter includes five. As a result, complex bodies are usually developed in the W. Shandong upwarped area which are mainly controlled by NE- and EW-trendingregional faults, while composite masses are widely distributed in the E.

Shandong upwarped area which are chiefly controlled by NE- or NNE-tre-nding regional faults, On the other hand, the volcanic-intrusive complexes.are predominant in the Yishu fault zone which are basically controlled byNNE-trending regionai faults.

In Shandong Province, the magmatic rocks have been evolved continuo-usly and irreversibly with respect to the lithology, rock-forming minerals,accessory mineral associations, petrochemistry, trace and rare earth elementsearly basic rocks to the later acid ones which is also reflected by the vari-ations in the amounts of major rock-forming minerals-potash feldspar andplagioclase- and the changes in the An content of plagioclase. There is aconsiderable difference between the pre-Yanshanian and the Yanshanianintrusive rocks: the former contain more plagioclase with higher An content(normally greater than 30) but less or very little potash-feldspar, whereasthe latter, especially granites, enrich the potash-feldspar content which isnearly equal to or more than the plagioclase content as the predominantphase in the rocks with the An content of plagioclase becoming less(often less than 30).So far as the composite granite mass is concerned, fromthe early inttusions to the later ones the amount of plagioclase and its Anyalues decrease.

The magmatic rocks in Shandong Province have formed from variouspreliminarily into three genetic series, i. e. the mantle-derived series, theanatectic genetic series of mixed origin and the crust-transformed geneticseries, and some subseries. The predominant one is the anatectic geneticseries of mixed origin, or especially, the remelting genetic subseries of mixedorigin, and secondly, the crust-ttansformed genetic series (mainly distributedin W. Shandong). The three series, particularly the latte two, tend to evolvein parallel and are related to each other.

4. According to the basic principles and approaches of Li Siguang's.Geomechanics, the structures in Shandong Province can be classified into thelatitudinal structure systen, the regional EW-trending structures, the reg-ional NS-tending structures, the Neocathaysian System, the Cathaysian.structures, the West Shandong vortex structure, the North Shandong brushstructure and the East Shandong "a"-type structure. Meanwhile, the ancientbasement structures are roughly discussed and the generation, development,incorporation-combination relationship of various structural systems and theircontrol over rocks and ore-deposits are analyzed and elaborated.

Moreover, the Yishu fault zone has been studied in a deep-going waywith its distribution, inner structures, dynamic features and geophysical cha-racteristics having been expounded in great detail and its forning history

also analyzed. In addition, the important views (with dispute up to now)and the research history on the fault zone are summarized. Some believed that it came into being in theArchaean or Proterozoic and moved for a long time; others considered it asa fault zone formed in the Mesozoic, which underwent mainly the left-handedstrike-slip movement(s), but there are still different opinions on the distance of its displacement.

5. The geological development history of Shandong has been systematically described in terms of four evolutionary stages (the Archaean-Proterozoic, the Palaeozoic, the Mesozoic and the Cenozoic) on the basis of crustalmovements and geological processes. For the Archaean-Proterozoic stage, emphasis is put on the analyses of the geologic events and its evolution inShandong mainly according to the characteristics of deposition, magmatism,metamorphism, migmatization and tectonism as evidenced from the ArchaeanTaishan Group, the Lower Proterozoic Jining Group and the Upper Proterozoic Tumen Group of the Qingbaikou System in W. Shandong and fromthe Archaean-Proterozoic Jiaodong and Jiaonan groups, the Lower Proterozoic Fenzishan and Wulian groups and the Upper Proterozoic Penglai Groupin E. Shandong. For the Palaeozoic, when the crust in Shandong was relatively stable but with frequent oscillatory movements, discussion is mainlyfocused on the sedimentary facies and ancient environment changes. For theMeso-Cenozoic time when the crust in the region was in an activization state,the characteristics of sedimentation, magmatism, mineralization and formation and development of tectonic systems are discussed in accordance withthe Geomechanics.

Thanks to the joint efforts made by the mass of geologists both within theprovince and beyond, a great deal of new progress and knowledge on the regional geology of Shandong has been achieved. However, it is worth while to notethat some problems remain to be further studied in the future, which includethose, for example, whether the supracrustal rocks below the Taishan Groupunderlie the Yanlingguan Formation or the Wanshanzhuang Formation; whether the Jurassic Fenshuiling and Laiyang formations should be assigned to theCretaceous or not; the gneiss and the age of the Linglong and Kunyushangranites; the relationship between the Jiaodong (or Jiaonan) Group andthe Fenzishan Group; the formation time and evolution of the Yishu faultzone, etc.
